bib.title: A Plan Reuse Mechanism for LLM-Driven Agent

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "A Plan Reuse Mechanism for LLM-Driven Agent" (AgentReuse), Guopeng Li, Ruiqi Wu, Haisheng Tan (USTC). arXiv:2512.21309v2 [cs.MA], 25 Dec 2025. English version of a 2024 paper in the Journal of Computer Research and Development (crad.ict.ac.cn). Not peer-reviewed in this form.

COVERAGE: All 11 pages. I read the extraction in four overlapping chunks, about 64,447 chars in all: the abstract, body, experiments, discussion, conclusion and the start of the references. I skimmed the references for origins only. There are no appendices. Figures 4, 5 and 6 are plots, so their values are unreadable from the extraction. Only the tables and prose numbers are quoted.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Plan reuse costs about 24 ms and removes plan generation latency, which is the main saving.
  number: 93.12% less latency than no reuse; 60.61% less than GPTCache. The 93.12% rests on assumed latencies, not a measured end-to-end run.
  setup: SMP dataset. Assumes 31.8 s per LLM plan call, with every non-true-positive request regenerating its plan. Execution latency is excluded.
  quote: "Compared to the LLM response caching method GPTCache, AgentReuse reduces latency by 60.61%." Also: "Therefore, compared to no reuse, AgentReuse reduces latency by 93.12%."
  where: §6.5, p.9
- Stripping the key parameters before comparing requests, and searching only within the intent class, beats comparing raw request text.
  number: F1 0.9718 and accuracy 0.9459 for AgentReuse. GPTCache scores 0.9100 and 0.8366. This is +6.8 and +13.06 percentage points. WithArgs (raw text) scores 0.9035 and 0.8272.
  setup: SMP dataset, 2,664 requests (the text also says 2,644), 23 intents, threshold γ=0.75, m3e-small embeddings, FAISS IndexFlatIP.
  quote: "Table 1: Experimental Results for Similarity Evaluation (γ= 0.75) … AgentReuse 0.9718 0.9931 0.9513 0.9459"
  where: §6.3, Table 1, p.7
- Plan reuse gives the same answer as regenerating the plan in 93 of 100 trials.
  number: 93 of 100 identical, so a 93% effective reuse rate.
  setup: AutoGen, 20 requests, 5 repeats each. The reused structured plan with swapped parameters is compared with a fresh plan.
  quote: "In 93 tests, the responses were identical, indicating an effective reuse rate of 93%."
  where: §6.3, p.8
- About 30% of agent requests are identical or similar. This is the motivating premise. It is cited from earlier work (Gill et al. [13], and the dataset in [40]) and not measured here.
  number: about 30%
  quote: "Analysis of the personal assistant dataset in [13] and [40] indicates that about 30% of task requests in LLM-driven agents are semantically identical or similar."
  where: §1, p.1-2
- Generating a plan is slow, which is the cost reuse removes.
  number: 31.8 s average plan generation (100 tests, GPT-4 via AutoGen). The intro example takes about 25 s, 2015 tokens and $0.073.
  quote: "the average plan generation latency is 31.8s."
  where: §4, p.4
- A wrong cache hit means a wrong action, so the paper reuses the plan and not the response. Time, origin and destination differ per request, and flight data changes.
  number: none. Its demonstration is a raw-text similarity at 0.75 that calls "Hefei to Beijing" and "Changsha to Shanghai" dissimilar.
  quote: "this paper reuses the plan rather than the response."
  where: §1 and §4, p.2 and p.5
- Precision is already high for the baselines, and recall is where raw text loses. At γ=0.75, GPTCache has precision 0.9887 and recall 0.8428, and MeanCache has precision 0.9991 and recall 0.4506. Raising γ from 0.75 to 0.95 raises precision and lowers recall.
  quote: "as the threshold increases, Recall and Accuracy gradually decrease, while Precision gradually increases."
  where: §6.3, p.7. The curves are in Fig. 4 and not readable as text.
- The intent-scoped search is cheaper than an unscoped one, and about equally accurate.
  number: OneIntent F1 0.9712 and accuracy 0.9444. It has 17.66% higher latency overall and 47.94% higher search latency. The paper says it also lets some non-reusable requests through, which lowers precision.
  setup: Latency over 50 tests. AgentReuse totals 23.489 ms per request and GPTCache 11.528 ms.
  quote: "OneIntent's similarity search latency is 47.94% higher than AgentReuse because it searches all cached content"
  where: §6.4.2, p.8
- Overhead is small, but the figure is partly inconsistent.
  number: about 100 MB extra VRAM and about 9.206 ms per request if an intent classifier already exists. About 500 MB VRAM and 23.489 ms otherwise. Each vector is 2 KB (512 dimensions at 4 B). Each plan is under 1 KB.
  quote: "AgentReuse would bring about 100 MB of extra VRAM cost and about 9.206 ms of processing latency per request."
  where: §6.4, p.8-9

LIMITS
- Every number comes from a Chinese-language personal-assistant request set (SMP) and one embedder (m3e-small). Only the 20-request subset has actual agent execution.
- The latency gain is arithmetic from an assumed 31.8 s per plan, with execution time excluded.
- The authors say it is "exploratory" and may not handle real, more complex tasks. Multi-intent and causally linked requests need new models (§7.1). Structured-plan extraction relies on prompting the LLM to annotate step dependencies. Serverless container tracing is future work.
- The 2,664 versus 2,644 request count is inconsistent. So are "other latencies … do not exceed 1 ms (all are 5.228 ms)" and the §6 intro's "latency is reduced by 60.61 percentage points". These are extraction or authoring faults, not mine.
- There is no ablation of the threshold's effect on bad plan reuse in agent runs, only on the similarity classification.
- The "30% similar" premise is borrowed. The paper does not say what share of the 2,664 requests are reusable.

BUILDS ON
- GPTCache: Fu Bang, NLP-OSS 2023 (baseline).
- MeanCache: Gill et al. [13], PCA to 64 dimensions (baseline).
- Zhu et al. [61], theory of LLM response caching.
- AutoGen [53].
- Intent and slot filling: Ma et al. 2024 [30], IEEE TNNLS. Models: bert-base-chinese [14] and m3e-small [37].
- FAISS [33].
- The SMP dataset [39] and the personal-agent dataset [40].
- KV-cache lineage: PagedAttention (Kwon, SOSP 2023), H2O, CacheGen (SIGCOMM 2024), HotPrefix and IMPRESS (FAST 25).
- NIRVANA approximate caching (Agarwal et al., NSDI 2024).

CODE: Algorithm 1 (p.4), paraphrased from the extraction.
- For each request, embed it and run intent classification plus parameter identification.
- If the intent is defined, remove the parameters to get q⁻ and E(q⁻), then search the cache within that intent.
- If the best score is ≥ γ, execute the matched plan with the new parameters. Otherwise generate a plan with the LLM, execute it, and store ⟨E(q⁻), plan, intent⟩.
- The IndexFlatIP implementation needs normalised vectors, as the text states: "the vectors need to be normalized first."
- The default is γ = 0.75, an empirical value.

FIGURES (caption text only; none rendered)
- Fig. 2, p.5: flowchart of AgentReuse. Intent classification, parameter extraction, similarity check and cache, with the reuse and not-reusable branches. It is the clearest single picture of the design.
- Fig. 4, p.7: F1, precision, recall and accuracy against threshold γ for five methods. It shows the precision-recall tradeoff as the threshold moves.
- Fig. 5, p.8: per-request similarity scores for AgentReuse and WithArgs, with the threshold line. It shows how removing parameters raises scores for requests that should be reused.
- Fig. 6, p.8: per-request latency split into intent classification, similarity lookup and other, for the five methods.
- Fig. 3, p.6: execution graph for the 7-step travel plan.

FIT TO NOTES
- `notes/10-semantic-cache.md` is the target note. It already cites GPTCache (Bang, 2023). Its tiering, threshold 0.85, and false-hit and guard-list sections cover response caching. A grep of the notes found no mention of AgentReuse, plan caching or MeanCache. The finding is new to the note and not yet claimed.
- The best fit is next to the false-hit and guard-list discussion (around line 220). It shows an academic version of the same hazard. Raw-text similarity wrongly rejects or wrongly accepts requests that differ only in slots, and the paper's fix is to remove the parameters and scope the search by intent.
- Caveats for the note:
  - It is a plan cache for agents, not an answer cache for RAG.
  - It tests on Chinese assistant commands, not support questions.
  - Its latency gain depends on an assumed 31.8 s per plan.
- The Tallybook note's own measured numbers use a different task, so do not mix them with this paper's.
- `references.md` does not list the paper. It needs a row, and the `[10]` link and note anchor should go in the right-hand column.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The figure axis text is garbled (font-encoded) and the Fig. 4 data points are unreadable. The inconsistencies noted under LIMITS come from the paper. I did not run the figures script. I have no CLI access to the ledger. I changed no files.
